mechanism: Pair each part's two outer sides by actual equal-length opposite-side families and identify their complete common jagged boundary. Targets transferring matched boundary length to equal area (E), a perimeter-versus-area misconception. The colored jagged path is the one existing division; it does not add a division or constrain its location.
mathematical_solution: Let opposite outer-side lengths be a and b, and let the arbitrary common jagged path length be L. Each part has perimeter a+b+L, so D always holds. The dividing path can move within the parallelogram while its endpoints remain opposite vertices; moving a portion changes one part area and the other oppositely, so equal area need not hold. In the actual frozen diagram the jagged cut is not a straight diagonal, and its asymmetric excursions are unchanged and visible. The other perimeter inequalities contradict equality, and no area inequality holds for every legal path. D remains the unique universally true choice.
